title: BMP (exact CPU state of the art) vs the exact GPU scorers on the full collection, same host
status: protocol registered 2026-11-17; no recorded run yet
question: How does BMP compare with the exact GPU scorers on the same host, index, queries and answers, at full scale?
hypothesis: None about the size of the gap; replaces a cross-paper indication with a same-host measurement.
motivation: The only state-of-the-art comparison so far is BMP's published 10.5 ms mean against our GPU means on other hardware; the team validated BMP at 100K and 1M only.

declared_changes.bmp: pinned BMP 67ad8c68 with the team's reviewed canonical patch and resident overlay; new single-index adapter whose timed query() is byte-identical to the validated adapter
declared_changes.gpu: no new GPU timing; compared with range-pruning run 20261117-cuda5-prune-04

correctness_rule: BMP's ordered (original_id, score) top-10 equals the pinned CPU reference for every query, in correctness and in every timing process.
success_rule: A complete run under the registered protocol; the result is reported whatever the ratios are.
failure_rule: Any mismatch, rejected expected run, or failure other than an ineligible (contended or paging) process.
